title: Hecke Base Change, Semisimplicity, and Deformation

items.title: Finite Hecke specialization and its regular-trace determinant
items.statement: For finite W over a characteristic-zero field k, construct the universal Laurent-coefficient Hecke algebra and define the Gram matrix of (x,y) ↦ Tr(L_xy) in its standard basis. Its determinant specializes to the regular-trace determinant of every field fiber and changes by a nonzero square under a field-basis change.

references.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL course notes
references.locator: §§2 and 4.1, PDF pp. 6–7 and 15–16: finite Coxeter Hecke basis, the canonical trace, coefficient specialization, and the generic semisimplicity context.

references.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations
references.locator: §1.1, PDF pp. 4–5: normalized finite Hecke relations, the symmetric trace, finite-dimensional deformation, and the rank-one exceptional case.

items.title: The one-parameter formal-series ring is complete, separated, and has residue field $k$
items.statement: For a field k and R=k\llbracket h\rrbracket, prove R/hR is canonically k, R is a domain and h-adically complete and separated, finite free modules are complete, and Frac(R) is a field.

references.title: Benjamin Sambale, An Invitation to Formal Power Series, author-hosted full-text notes
references.locator: §2, Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2, PDF pp. 2–3: coefficient-sequence definition, Cauchy convolution, and domain argument; the local proof derives residue and h-adic facts explicitly.

references.title: Herbert S. Wilf, generatingfunctionology, author-hosted second-edition PDF
references.locator: §2.1, listed at printed p. 30 in the source table of contents; the relevant full-text pages were not retrievable in this run.

items.title: Finite direct summands over a formal-series ring are free with rank read from reduction
items.statement: The image of an idempotent endomorphism of k\llbracket h\rrbracket^n is free of finite rank r, where r is the k-dimension of its reduction modulo h, including rank zero.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Structure of Finite Dimensional Algebras, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.712, Chapter 7
references.locator: §7.1, Theorem 7.1 and Definition 7.2, PDF p. 1: projective modules as direct summands of free modules; the local determinant argument proves the formal-series freeness and rank statement.

items.axiom_use: No arbitrary Choice beyond a basis of a finite-dimensional vector space and finitely many lifts.

items.title: Orthogonal idempotents lift over a complete formal power-series ring
items.statement: In a finite free algebra over k\llbracket h\rrbracket, every finite complete orthogonal idempotent family modulo h lifts to a complete orthogonal family in the algebra by explicit h-adic Newton corrections and complementary corners.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Structure of Finite Dimensional Algebras, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.712, Chapter 7
references.locator: §7.2, Proposition 7.3 and Corollary 7.5, PDF p. 1: idempotent lifting through nilpotent ideals and lifting a complete orthogonal family; the local proof establishes the stronger complete k\llbracket h\rrbracket case by Newton iteration.

items.axiom_use: No arbitrary Choice. The input family and every corner induction are finite.

items.title: A nondegenerate regular-trace pairing forces semisimplicity
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional algebra over a field, nondegeneracy of (x,y) ↦ Tr(L_xy) forces its left regular module to be semisimple. The proof identifies the two Jacobson-radical descriptions, proves radical nilpotence by a composition series, and uses finite maximal-left-ideal descent without arbitrary Choice.

references.title: Arun Ram, Lectures in Representation Theory, Lecture 5
references.locator: Theorem 1.41 and Definition 1.44, lines 13–24: the regular trace, Gram matrix, and the stated finite-dimensional criterion; the local item supplies the full radical proof independently.

references.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations
references.locator: §1.1, PDF p. 5: finite-dimensional Hecke semisimplicity and the Jacobson-radical formulation, with the exact proof route independently supplied locally.

items.axiom_use: No arbitrary Choice. The finite maximal-left-ideal descent uses at most dim_K(H) successive witness selections.

items.title: Matrix units lift through a finite free split formal deformation
items.statement: If A is finite free over k\llbracket h\rrbracket and A/hA is a finite product of full matrix algebras over k, then A is isomorphic to the product of full matrix algebras of the same sizes over k\llbracket h\rrbracket, via lifts of the reduction's matrix units.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Structure of Finite Dimensional Algebras, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.712, Chapter 7
references.locator: §7.2, Proposition 7.3, Corollary 7.5 and §7.3, Theorem 7.6, PDF pp. 1–2: lifting primitive diagonal idempotents and organizing projective matrix blocks; the local proof constructs all matrix units over k\llbracket h\rrbracket.

items.axiom_use: No arbitrary Choice. Only finitely many matrix units, corner bases, and coordinates are selected.

items.title: Finite Coxeter Hecke algebras are semisimple over the generic characteristic-zero field
items.statement: For finite W and a characteristic-zero coefficient field k, the regular-trace determinant of the generic finite Hecke algebra is a nonzero Laurent polynomial. Hence the algebra over the fraction field is semisimple; every field specialization where that determinant is nonzero is also semisimple.

references.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL course notes
references.locator: §4.1 and Theorems 4.2–4.4, PDF pp. 15–16: finite Coxeter Hecke specializations, generic split semisimplicity, and character deformation; proofs cited there are not imported as substitutes for the local trace argument.

references.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations
references.locator: §1.1, PDF pp. 4–5: finite Hecke Tits deformation, the polynomial semisimplicity locus, and the rank-one exceptional case.

items.axiom_use: No arbitrary Choice. The regular trace basis and the finite group basis are fixed by the standard basis.

items.title: Split formal deformations preserve simple-block labels; the trace determinant bounds exceptional parameters
items.statement: A finite free k\llbracket h\rrbracket deformation of a split semisimple finite-dimensional k-algebra has the same full matrix blocks in the generic and special fibers, giving a label bijection for their simple modules. For finite Hecke specializations, determinant nonvanishing is a sufficient semisimplicity condition; its zero locus is only the exceptional set of this certificate unless a separate converse is proved.

references.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL course notes
references.locator: §4.1 and Theorems 4.2–4.4, PDF pp. 15–16: split generic Hecke semisimplicity and Tits-style character correspondence under stated hypotheses.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Structure of Finite Dimensional Algebras, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.712, Chapter 7
references.locator: §7.2–7.3, PDF pp. 1–2: orthogonal idempotent lifting and the matrix-block organization of simple modules; the local formal theorem proves its stronger complete-ring statement.

items.axiom_use: No arbitrary Choice. Each block label comes from the finite index set of matrix factors.

title: Hecke Base Change, Semisimplicity, and Deformation — Examples

items.title: A rank-one Hecke algebra with a perfect symmetrizing form and degenerate regular trace
items.statement: The rank-one normalized Hecke algebra at v=i is not semisimple although its canonical symmetrizing-trace pairing is perfect; its regular-trace determinant is zero.

references.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations
references.locator: §1.1, PDF pp. 4–5: the rank-one finite Hecke algebra at unnormalized parameter q=−1 and the repeated-root nonsemisimple algebra; the local verification computes both trace forms explicitly.

references.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL course notes
references.locator: §2 and §4.1, PDF pp. 6–7 and 15–16: canonical Hecke trace and finite specialization conventions; the local example independently computes the rank-one forms.

items.title: Explicitly lifting the two simple labels in a formal rank-two algebra
items.statement: For A=Q\llbracket h\rrbracket[X]/(X²−(1+h)²), the special and generic fibers are both split products of two fields, with the same labels exhibited by explicit lifted orthogonal idempotents.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Structure of Finite Dimensional Algebras, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.712, Chapter 7
references.locator: §7.2, Corollary 7.5, PDF p. 1: lifting complete orthogonal idempotents; the example verifies the complete formal-series lift directly.

references.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL course notes
references.locator: §4.1, PDF p. 15: the finite-Hecke formal deformation and label-correspondence context; the example is a direct two-dimensional model.
